newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech parliament approves balanced 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Czech parliament approves balanced 1997 budget.

text.p: The lower house of Czech parliament on Friday narrowly approved the government's draft 1997 state budget, with equal revenue and expenditure of 549.1 billion crowns, up from the revised 1996 budget of 491 billion.
The final vote on the minority government's plan was approved with the minimum required 99 deputies in the 200-seat chamber voting in favour, 96 against, and five not voting.

Out of 23 line-item amendments put to a vote before the final package was approved, only three spending increases on the government draft were accepted totalling 122.55 million crowns, including an additional 100 million for the agriculture ministry budget.

It kept the corporate income tax rate at 39 percent, killing a junior coalition party's move to lower it to 35 percent, and extended the required period for holding securities before a waiver on capital gains tax takes effect to six months from three.

The coalition led by Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) fell two seats short of a majority in the 200-seat Chamber in June elections, and the budget vote was seen as crucial to the survival of the minority government.
But in October four members of the opposition Social Democrats broke party ranks to allow the draft 1997 budget to get through the parliament's first reading.
